items.title_found: Resolution of Erdős Problem #728: a writeup of Aristotle’s Lean proof
passages: Alexeev, Lean formalization of Erdős Problem #728 (Erdos728b.lean), in the repository lean-proofs, https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos728b.lean, accessed 2026-01-27. [2] T.
The system in question is a combination of GPT-5.2 Pro by OpenAI and Aristotle by Harmonic, operated by Kevin Barreto.
On Jan 4, 2026, Kevin Barreto announced that he had a proof from the AI system: Aristotle by Harmonic.

Specific to producing this writeup: Boris Alexeev ran Aristotle to simplify the proof; Kevin Barreto produced the original proofs; KoishiChan performed literature search; Terence Tao suggested further ideas and found extra literature.

Letting M→∞M\to\infty along an infinite sequence yields infinitely many triples. ∎ 6 Correspondence with the Lean development The accompanying Lean file Erdos728b.lean [1] contains a fully formal proof of the main theorem.
This is a Lean system, and the input to Aristotle was based on an informal argument from GPT-5.2 Pro.
But - on Jan 5, 2026, Barreto again asked GPT-5.2 Pro whether its argument could be upgraded to tackle the version that forum participants had now identified as the problem.
Thus, the current status is that Erdős Problem 728 was fully resolved autonomously by AI with no prior human literature resolving the problem found.
Appendix: beyond this proof Shortly after this proof was completed, Erdős problem #729 was then solved on Jan 10, 2026, and #401 on Jan 11, 2026, again autonomously by AI.
Barreto’s version resolved one version of the problem, but it wasn’t clear whether this was the intended version.
